text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any neck stiffness or sensitivity to light? Also, have you noticed any rigidity, tremors, or excessive sweating recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of haloperidol use and these specific symptoms, I suspect Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your significantly elevated creatine kinase confirms the diagnosis of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, likely triggered by your haloperidol use. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
